gaps.sentence: I'm afraid your passport is ___ — it expired last month (VALID).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: it has expired
gaps.explanation: An expired document is invalid (in- + valid); an adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: New technology has ___ the way we work (REVOLUTION).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: revolutionise. After 'has' the past participle 'revolutionised' is needed.

gaps.sentence: She showed great ___ in dealing with the crisis (ABLE).
gaps.explanation: After 'great' a positive noun is needed: ability (-ity); 'inability' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: He is very ___ about local history (KNOW).
gaps.explanation: 'Knowledgeable about something' means knowing a lot about it; it is the adjective form of 'knowledge'.

gaps.sentence: We must ___ our efforts to finish on time (STRONG).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: strengthen. A base verb follows 'must'.

gaps.sentence: We ___ the cost of the trip and ran out of money (ESTIMATE).
gaps.hint: judged it too low — that is why the money ran out (under-)
gaps.explanation: Running out of money shows the estimate was too low: underestimated (under- + estimated).

gaps.sentence: His sudden ___ came as a shock to everyone (DEPART).
gaps.hint: noun needed as subject (-ure); beware the word meaning 'part of an organisation'
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'depart' is departure (-ure); a department is a section of an organisation.

gaps.sentence: The airline is known for its excellent ___ (SERVE).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'excellent'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'serve' is 'service' (-ice); a servant is a person who serves.
